A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NABLA benchmark and proxy-identity training framework. Their main texts, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on NABLA, iNat-Seen, and iNat-Unseen in Table 1, plus caption ablations and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Individual-Birds evaluation and mixed-control results in Tables A4 and A5.

M1.justification: v1 discusses combining depth and fill as a possible extension. v2 implements an experimental variant that pastes depth-map pixels into the masked bird region of the fill image and fine-tunes OminiControl with FLUX-Kontext (Appendix C.4, Figure A5). The core architectures and proxy-pair training procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on Individual-Birds from WildlifeReID-10k, excluding Zebra Finches (Appendix C.3). This extends coverage to another source of same-individual bird images while retaining the original training data, three evaluation datasets, and bird-generation task.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain Insert Anything, Omini-S, Nano Banana, and GPT-4V. Table A4 reuses existing Insert Anything and Omini-S baselines on the added dataset; no new external comparison method is introduced. Figure 2's GPT-Vision label becomes GPT-4V.

E3.justification: The new Individual-Birds evaluation uses WildlifeReID-10k validation and test sets, samples three random image pairs per individual, and excludes Zebra Finches (Appendix C.3). The original evaluation metrics, splits, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 and Table A5 add a focused ablation testing whether combining depth and fill improves on either control alone. The existing caption-length ablation, correlation analyses, and qualitative failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing correlation reporting is unchanged. The three image pairs per individual in the new evaluation specify sample selection, not repeated experimental runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and A2 retain identical values. New Table A4 reports Individual-Birds results: Insert Anything DINO increases from 0.77 to 0.81 after fine-tuning, but Omini-S MSE worsens from 22.3 to 24.3 for fill and 25.1 to 26.6 for depth. Table A5 adds mixed-control scores, including DINO 0.77 and MSE 57.0, versus 0.78 and 51.0 for fill alone; its separate-control rows reproduce existing results.

T1.justification: No formal definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The metric descriptions and proxy-identity rationale remain unchanged; the mixed-control addition is procedural and empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same benchmark, proxy-training, unseen-species generalization, and visualization claims, including the stated 41% MSE reduction. The additional experiments do not redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: v1 suggests that combining depth and fill could mitigate their weaknesses. v2 qualifies this suggestion with evidence that simple combination provides little improvement (Section 4.3 and Appendix C.4). Appendix C.3 also interprets Individual-Birds results as showing similar improvement trends, although Table A4 contains Omini-S MSE regressions.

D1.justification: v2 identifies annotators as volunteers with over eight years of field experience (Appendix A.1). Appendix B.3 newly specifies proprietary-model execution dates, public website use, and Pro/default modes; the prompt itself was already in v1. The introduction now reports the dataset and benchmarking code as available rather than planned for release.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the OpenCows2020 discussion with WildlifeReID-10k, adds the Individual-Birds reference, and replaces the Nano Banana blog citation with the Gemini 2.5 report. New Appendix A.5 expands comparisons with existing generation and animal-identification datasets. Most remaining reference changes update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and caption edits, adds acknowledgments, and introduces appendix subsections for dataset comparisons, proprietary-model settings, and the two new experiments. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables A4 and A5 and a mixed-control illustration in Figure A5. The original Figure A1 moves to Figure A9, with other appendix figures renumbered. Figure 2 is reformatted and recropped, and Figure 8 gains observer credits. Most existing visual content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens the paper through additional same-individual evaluation, an empirical test of the previously speculative control combination, and clearer reproducibility information. The core evidence remains unchanged. The broad improvement summary in Appendix C.3 needs qualification because Omini-S MSE worsens, but this limitation does not outweigh the useful added validation and documentation.
